title: Summer Games
build: The PAL G64 of Epyx's disk (directory "SUMMER GAMES"): the boot file SUMMER GAMES and SGLOAD, the engine B unpacked to $0C00-$3EFF, the opening ceremony A, six event files D, E, F, H, I and K each unpacked over $4000 upward (swimming over $1000-$BEFF), the world records WR and DEFAULT, and the unused files L and M; a second PAL image and an NTSC image were supplied too

The front end's entry (module 0, file A), reached from the boot loader and from main-menu item 6: the opening ceremony. Banks the BASIC ROM out (bit 0 of $01), sets up the raster interrupt (cer_irq_setup), the screen and the sprites (cer_screen_setup), stops the ceremony's state machine at stage 0, starts the SID (cer_sound_init) and the fanfare (tune 2), then waits with interrupts on until the tune ends ($1E = $FF) and jumps to boot_restart, which goes to the engine's main menu.

Raster interrupt at line $FB (bottom of the screen), the main step of the ceremony, once a frame. Plays the next step of the fanfare (cer_music_step), counts frames at $7F7C, puts the eight sprites of the lower band (the doves) on the chip from the shadow tables at $7F57 (positions), $7F6B (colours) and $7F73 (shapes), then branches on the stage in $7F7F: stage 1 runs cer_flare, stage 2 cer_burn, stage 3 turns every lower sprite on and goes on as stage 0. Stage 0 walks the torch-bearer: the upper band's X positions (the X bytes of the pairs from $7F32) step down by one a frame, the X high bit flips when they pass zero, and stage 1 starts when they reach $4E with the high bit clear, stage 2 when they reach 0; the running frame ($7F7D) cycles every four frames and picks three shapes from cer_torch_frames. Then flies the doves (cer_doves), puts the flame's shapes into the upper band's shadow ($7F52-$7F55), and chains to cer_irq_mid at line $6E.

Fly the eight doves: each has a countdown at $7EFF reloaded from $7EF7 that lifts it a pixel when it runs out, a fixed-point horizontal speed added from $7EEF through $7F07, the X high bit toggled in $7F67 when it wraps, and a wing frame chosen from its X position (shapes $D3-$D7 at $7EE7). A dove that climbs above line $5C is switched off in $7F7B. Also makes the torch's flame flicker by writing random bytes from cer_random straight into its shape, $C2, at $7080 and $7083.

Raster interrupt at line $6E: puts the upper band's sprites (the runner, the torch and its flame, from the shadow tables at $7F32, $7F3A, $7F46 and $7F4E) on the chip, re-arms cer_irq_top at line $FB and leaves through the KERNAL-free exit at $77E0 (pull Y, X, A and RTI).

Stage 1, the lighting of the bowl: steps through the five frames of cer_flare_tab, counting $7F81 down from each frame's time and $7F80 down through the frames, placing the flame and setting the shapes; parks the lower band's sprites at X and Y $FF meanwhile. When the last frame runs out sets stage 3 and lets the doves fly. Goes on to cer_doves
Stage 2: shows the upper band's sprites ($7F56 = $F0) and every lower sprite, then flies the doves.
Turn off CIA 1's interrupts, enable the raster interrupt at line $FB and point the IRQ vector at cer_irq_top; bitmap mode on ($D011 = $3B).

Set the ceremony's picture: multicolour bitmap in video bank 1 ($4000; screen at $6000, bitmap at $4000), colour RAM from $6400-$67FF, background dark grey, border black; then the sprites' start positions, colours and shapes in the shadow tables, sprite multicolours red and yellow.
The ceremony's random-number step: shifts and mixes the two bytes at $18/$19 and returns a new byte in A. The same generator as the engine's random ($1661), with its state in zero page.
Clear the SID, give the three voices attack/decay $21 and sustain/release $84, volume 15 and pulse width $0400, and mark no tune playing ($1E = $FF) with the pointer at the silent record $7DC8.
Start tune Y (an offset into the tune table at $7B16) unless a tune with a lower number is already playing: sets the note pointer $1B/$1C and clears the note timer $1D.

One frame of the fanfare player. While the note timer $1D runs, counts it down and releases the three gates in its last five frames. Then reads the next four-byte record: three note numbers (indexes into the frequency tables at $7DC9/$7DF9; a first byte of 0 leaves all three voices as they are) and a length index into $7E29; a negative first byte ends the tune (frequencies zeroed, $1E = $FF). Voices 1 and 2 play a sawtooth ($21), voice 3 a pulse wave ($41).
Two pointers into the tunes: $7C6F (a tune the ceremony never starts) and $7B1A, the fanfare (tune 2).
The fanfare's pointer, high bytes ($7B17 for tune 0, and on with tune 2's)
The ceremony fanfare: four-byte records, three note numbers and a length index, ending with $FF.
A second tune in the ceremony's table, the same notes as the engine's tune at $3928; the ceremony only ever starts tune 2.
The record the player points at between tunes: no notes, length index 1, then the end marker.

Text nothing reads: "SUMMER GAMES" in reversed letters, then "COPYRIGHT (C) 1983  EPYX", each ended by $FF. The title screen says 1984.
